Autocomplete to agents in under four years. Autocomplete. Chat. Agents.
The tools have always changed. We adapt to use them.
Are our roles changing? Absolutely!
But first... What does a Software Engineer actually do?
Write Code. Go Home. …right?
How many hours a day do you actually get to code?
How many hours would you prefer to spend coding?

What a Software Engineer really does Requirements & Planning System Design & Architecture Writing Code Testing & Debugging Code Review Deployment & CI/CD Monitoring & Performance Communication & Collaboration Security & Compliance Documentation Mentoring & Leadership Problem Solving Writing code is just one piece of the puzzle
From the outside, the job looks like typing. Typing was always the smallest part.
The job didn't change. The role expanded.
Not everybody is going to make that transition. If your whole job was one narrow thing, that part is going away.
If you really enjoyed carefully placing brackets and semicolons…
There are…challenges ahead.
If you love to build and create?
The world is your oyster!
A super technical product manager. Moving up the value chain. That's a good thing. Knowing what to ask. What to build. Which questions matter.
Where's the next bottleneck? • A week before: mostly writing code. • A week now: deciding, specifying, reviewing, running. • When writing code gets cheap, the bottleneck moves.
Are you measuring the impact?
Or are you measuring adoption?
AI allows you to generate code faster.
That doesn’t necessarily translate to more software.

DORA’s 2025 report crystallized the reality: AI is an ampli er of your development practices. Good processes get better (highperforming teams saw 55-70% faster delivery). Bad processes get worse (accumulating debt at unprecedented speed). There is no silver bullet. fi https://addyosmani.com/blog/the-80-problem-in-agentic-coding/
I don't write much code anymore. I write code to learn. I write code to teach. When I build, I review, I set gates, and I use what I know to build the right thing.
If you're attached to the code, you might be in trouble. If you love building things, you're going to be fine.

A wonderful time to be a builder! The old reality The new reality The superpower Great ideas, but no time, no budget, no team. Projects stayed on the backlog forever. Building anything meaningful took a big investment. You have an idea? Build it. Today. Tools for yourself, side projects, prototypes: things you couldn't touch before. The cost of trying things has collapsed. Fundamentals plus AI: an engineer who can build anything. You're not being replaced. You're being ampli ed. fi I don't think I've ever been this excited to build software!
